name: orderflow
extraInstructions:
### Verify Behavior With Fresh Data (write scenario)
Do not rely solely on existing database rows to infer business rules and
history/audit-trail behavior. Perform this minimal write scenario through the
UI (`web_ui__*` tools), then confirm what actually happened via the
`postgres__query` tool. Use exactly these fixed identifiers, not a unique
email per run — a separate cleanup step outside your control removes this
data after you finish, so the fixed identifiers are always free to reuse:

1. Create a new Customer: name "Discovery Test Customer", email
   "discovery-test@example.com".
2. Create a new Product: name "Discovery Test Product", price 19.99.
3. Create a new Order (DRAFT) for that customer with one item using that product.
4. Immediately query `OrderStatusHistory` for that new order's id — record
   exactly how many rows exist and their statuses right after creation
   (before any status change). Do not assume; report what you observed.
5. Submit the order (DRAFT → SUBMITTED) via the UI.
6. Query `OrderStatusHistory` again for that order — record the full,
   ordered sequence of entries (status + relative order).

Do not attempt to delete the Order, Product, or Customer yourself — a
SUBMITTED order cannot be deleted via the API or reverted to DRAFT (this is
correct, intentional application behavior), and your postgres tool is
read-only. A separate, non-agent cleanup step handles removing this test
data; trying to delete it yourself only wastes turns.

Record the exact sequence of OrderStatusHistory entries you observed at each
point (after create, after submit) in `businessRules` — write the concrete
observed sequence, not a generic statement like "tracks status changes".
cleanupSql: DELETE FROM "OrderStatusHistory" WHERE "orderId" IN (SELECT "Order".id FROM "Order" JOIN "Customer" ON "Order"."customerId" = "Customer".id WHERE "Customer".email = 'discovery-test@example.com')
DELETE FROM "OrderItem" WHERE "orderId" IN (SELECT "Order".id FROM "Order" JOIN "Customer" ON "Order"."customerId" = "Customer".id WHERE "Customer".email = 'discovery-test@example.com')
DELETE FROM "Order" WHERE "customerId" IN (SELECT id FROM "Customer" WHERE email = 'discovery-test@example.com')
DELETE FROM "Product" WHERE name = 'Discovery Test Product'
